doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Learning solos by ear: Pres and Hawkins
summary: He could play every Lester Young solo and Hawk's Body and Soul by ear, and his brother George sang them.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh man, we were all – I could play every solo Pres ever made, and I was working on Body and Soul when I got drafted. I could almost play Body and Soul by ear.
Yeah, Hawk’s solo. Everybody used to have me play his solo. They’d say, “Man, how’d you ever learn that thing?” I say, “That’s what I do.” I sit up and copy the cats I like solos.
How would you actually go about learning them? Did you . . .
Just by ear, and George could . . .
You’d just play it over and over on the record.
Yeah, and George could sing most of them.
Do you have to slow the record down or anything like that?

George had this great ear, and although he couldn’t play this solo, he said, “Man, you’re not playing it right.” He’s singing. I said, “Okay, George, thanks.” That’s a gift, but you can’t carry it too far.
